messages:
maria: Heads-up: sample-app edge build is failing typecheck. looks like ts overload resolution choking on our SDK generate signature.
devon: Can you paste the error? quick screenshot or copy-paste helps.
maria: "No overload matches this call. The last overload gave the following error..." when calling sdk.generate(parsedJson) where parsedJson: unknown from JSON.parse.
ryan: Edge ESM bundle emits different .d.ts layout than our CJS build. we've seen moduleResolution differences cause this.
maria: Locally changing tsconfig.moduleResolution to 'node' fixes it, but the template uses 'bundler' for edge runtimes.
devon: Hmm. The SDK has two overloads: a generic generate<T = any>(opts: GenerateOptions<T>) and a non-generic generate(opts: GenerateOptions<unknown>). overloads + unknown often confuse inference.
ryan: Suggestion: collapse to a single generic signature with `T = unknown` default so inference is consistent across bundlers. Less overloads = fewer surprises.
maria: That seems reasonable. any breaking concerns?
devon: Consumers that relied on a non-generic call will still work because generic with default will accept that shape. runtime stays identical.
ryan: Short-term: add a troubleshooting note in sample-app README: "If you hit overload errors in edge builds, try moduleResolution: 'node' or pin SDK >= patch." Also add a tiny helper type in examples to force inference.
maria: I'll open a tiny PR that consolidates overloads, add changelog entry, and update the sample-app docs. Also filing an issue to check d.ts emit differences between our Rollup/ESBuild edge pipeline and tsc for node.
ci-bot: CI: edge bundle typecheck failed on branch maria/edge-typing (exit 1) — https://ci.internal/edge-typing/42
maria: Thanks team — will iterate and keep this small. ping me if you see regressions.
